canonical.title: Microsoft 365 on Linux in 2026: what you actually lose

parent.title: Throwing away Windows: a replacement plan for an actual installed-software inventory

siblings.title: Your .NET + SQL Server stack on Linux: what actually replaces what
siblings.summary: Rider replaces Visual Studio + ReSharper on Linux at the cost of the WinForms/WPF designers; SQL Server itself moves cleanly to a container, but SSMS has no Linux successor now that Azure Data Studio is dead.

siblings.title: The utility belt: per-tool Linux verdicts for a Windows power user (2026)
siblings.summary: Per-tool verdicts for the Windows-only utilities in an actual installed-software inventory: most transfer cleanly, AutoHotkey and Power Automate Desktop have no single answer, and Wayland is the variable that decides the rest.

siblings.title: Multi-monitor, window management and the desktop shell: replacing DisplayFusion, Fences, FancyZones and X-Rite on Linux
siblings.summary: KDE Plasma 6.7 is the only Linux desktop that replaces most of DisplayFusion and FancyZones natively; Fences has no real equivalent and the X-Rite workflow becomes ArgyllCMS/DisplayCAL plus a per-screen ICC profile.

siblings.title: Gaming after the switch: your library survives, the NVIDIA App does not
siblings.summary: Both installed games run under Proton — Planetfall is Gold/Deck-Playable and Fall Guys' EAC is Linux-enabled — so the only hard loss is the NVIDIA App and Game Bar tooling layer, which becomes environment variables plus MangoHud and GPU Screen Recorder.

siblings.title: Legion hardware, peripherals and the two corporate VPNs on Linux
siblings.summary: Neither corporate VPN blocks the switch — Harmony SASE ships an official Linux agent and WatchGuard is reachable with plain OpenVPN; the real losses are QuantumENGINE, Dolby, XTU and Lenovo's AI/Space bloat.

siblings.title: Escape hatches for the leftovers: Wine, a VM, passthrough, or just keep the partition
siblings.summary: Wine for single-window utilities, a local Windows VM for Visual Studio and SSMS, RDP for the corporate cluster — and no GPU passthrough on a muxless Legion.

sources.title: https://github.com/abraunegg/onedrive
sources.claim: The OSS OneDrive client for Linux syncs Personal/Business/SharePoint libraries but explicitly does not implement Windows files-on-demand and is CLI-only.

sources.title: https://peterfalkingham.com/2026/03/04/office-365-and-linux-trying-to-use-linux-when-your-organization-is-all-in-and-locked-down-with-microsoft/
sources.claim: First-hand March 2026 account: Teams wrapper worked identically to Windows, DavMail/OWL solved mail+calendar, but the organisation blocked both popular open-source OneDrive clients from signing in and no client offers files-on-demand.

sources.title: https://obsidian.md/help/import/onenote
sources.claim: Obsidian's official OneNote importer supports only personal Microsoft accounts; work/school notebooks and locked sections cannot be imported.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/teams-client-desktop-admin
sources.claim: Microsoft's own Teams client availability matrix (updated 16 Jul 2026) marks Linux as not supported and lists Web as the supported route.

sources.title: https://discourse.gnome.org/t/is-microsoft-365-graph-api-expected-to-be-available-in-evolution-3-60-x/36019
sources.claim: Evolution maintainer confirms (3 Jul 2026) that Microsoft 365 Graph API accounts are available in Evolution 3.60.x via evolution-ews, past preview stage, but without full EWS feature parity.

sources.title: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/use-power-query-in-excel-for-the-web-02652946-de70-48d8-8a34-3db96998ff5a
sources.claim: Power Query in Excel for the web: viewing/refreshing for all Microsoft 365 subscribers, full authoring for Business/Enterprise plans, with a listed set of supported sources.

sources.title: https://www.acuitytraining.co.uk/news-tips/power-query-in-excel-for-the-web-whats-changed/
sources.claim: The full Power Query experience (import wizard plus editor) reached Excel for the web in January 2026; desktop still wins on local file sources, the full connector library and heavy M work.

sources.title: https://office-watch.com/2026/microsoft-office-linux/
sources.claim: 2026 survey of Office-on-Linux options: no native Office exists; browser Office is officially supported but VBA does not run; open-source suites break on complex layouts and macro-heavy files; a Windows VM is the power-user option.

sources.title: https://api.onlyoffice.com/docs/macros/guides/getting-started/
sources.claim: ONLYOFFICE macros are JavaScript against the Document Builder API, not VBA.

sources.title: https://blog.thunderbird.net/2025/11/thunderbird-adds-native-microsoft-exchange-email-support/
sources.claim: Thunderbird 145 shipped native Exchange (EWS) email support, removing the need for third-party add-ons for mail; calendar and address book remain on the roadmap.

sources.title: https://www.computerworld.com/article/4129036/after-years-of-warnings-microsoft-is-finally-pulling-the-plug-on-ews.html
sources.claim: EWS is disabled by default in Exchange Online on 1 Oct 2026 and fully shut down 1 Apr 2027; admin allow-lists must be configured before end of August 2026.

sources.title: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftteamsblog/microsoft-teams-progressive-web-app-now-available-on-linux/3669846
sources.claim: Microsoft announced GA of the Teams PWA for Linux as a feature of the web client.

sources.title: https://windowsforum.com/threads/davmail-6-8-adds-active-microsoft-graph-support-ready-for-ews-retirement.425710/
sources.claim: DavMail 6.8 exposes Microsoft Graph mode in the GUI with mandatory OAuth2 (MFA/Conditional Access compatible) and can auto-create Teams meetings via the CalDAV online-meeting setting.

sources.title: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1384944
sources.claim: Thunderbird cannot natively create invitations recognised as Microsoft Teams meetings; it is an open feature request.

sources.title: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/the-microsoft-365-app-transition-to-the-microsoft-365-copilot-app
sources.claim: The Microsoft 365 (Office) app became the Microsoft 365 Copilot app, reachable in any browser at m365.cloud.microsoft, with office.com and microsoft365.com redirecting.

sources.title: https://www.expandrive.com/blog/onedrive-and-sharepoint-on-linux-in-2023
sources.claim: There is no first-party OneDrive client for Linux; abraunegg is the gold-standard OSS daemon, onedriver has limited SharePoint support, and Insync is claimed to have dropped OneDrive in 2024.

sources.title: https://help.dropbox.com/installs/system-requirements
sources.claim: Dropbox's current Linux requirements: Ubuntu 18.04+/Fedora 28+, ext4, zfs, eCryptFS backed by ext4, xfs and btrfs, 64-bit only, no ARM.

sources.title: https://itsfoss.com/dropbox-linux-ext4-only/
sources.claim: In 2018 Dropbox announced it would sync only on ext4 on Linux from 7 November 2018.

sources.title: https://linuxreviews.org/Dropbox_will_again_support_filesystems_beyond_ext4
sources.claim: Dropbox partially reversed the ext4-only restriction in July 2019, re-adding zfs, eCryptFS, xfs and btrfs.

sources.title: https://blog.documentfoundation.org/blog/2026/02/04/libreoffice-26-2-is-here/
sources.claim: LibreOffice 26.2 was released 4 February 2026 with a focus on performance, interoperability and file formats.

sources.title: https://obsidian.md/download
sources.claim: Obsidian ships official Linux builds as AppImage, Snap, deb, Flatpak and an ARM64 AppImage.

sources.title: https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/07/claude-desktop-linux-beta
sources.claim: Anthropic released Claude Desktop for Linux in beta on 30 June 2026 for Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+ with an apt repo; Computer Use and voice dictation are missing.

sources.title: https://snapcraft.io/copilot-desktop
sources.claim: The Copilot Desktop snap for Linux is an unofficial community web wrapper published by Ken VanDine, last updated 9 February 2026.

sources.title: https://botmonster.com/self-hosting/wayland-screen-sharing-fix-video-calls-linux/
sources.claim: Wayland screen sharing needs three layers (xdg-desktop-portal backend, PipeWire, app pointed at portal capture); the Teams PWA in Chrome/Edge handles capture better than the Electron client.

sources.title: https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux/issues/2551
sources.claim: On Ubuntu 26 with GNOME/Wayland, screen sharing fails in the teams-for-linux snap build ('Bind context provider failed') while the .deb works, indicating snap confinement blocks the xdg-desktop-portal ScreenCast call.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/4433162/upload-custom-background-using-web-or-pwa-on-linux
sources.claim: Uploading custom meeting backgrounds is limited in the Teams web/PWA client on Linux, though blur and predefined backgrounds work.

sources.title: https://discussion.fedoraproject.org/t/microsoft-teams-pwa-background-filters-does-not-work/78500
sources.claim: Fedora users report Teams PWA background filters not working at all.

sources.title: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1116862/teams-pwa-notifications-on-linux
sources.claim: Long-running Microsoft Q&A thread documenting Teams PWA notification problems on Linux: silent notifications, toasts self-deleting after ~5 seconds, missing meeting-started alerts.

sources.title: https://github.com/IsmaelMartinez/teams-for-linux
sources.claim: teams-for-linux is an unofficial Electron wrapper of the Teams web app adding system notifications, tray, custom backgrounds, screen sharing and multi-account profiles, with contextIsolation and sandbox disabled.

sources.title: https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/exchange/retirement-of-exchange-web-services-in-exchange-online/3924440
sources.claim: Microsoft's official announcement of EWS retirement in Exchange Online, directing developers to Microsoft Graph.

sources.title: https://blog.thunderbird.net/2026/06/thunderbird-monthly-development-digest-june-2026/
sources.claim: June 2026: Thunderbird's Graph implementation is entering the final stretch toward EWS parity, calendar integration is only being planned, and Microsoft confirmed approved mail clients can obtain previously unavailable consent.

sources.title: https://roadmaps.thunderbird.net/en-US/desktop/
sources.claim: Thunderbird's desktop roadmap lists Exchange (EWS, GraphAPI) including calendar and address book as active work, with Exchange email support shipped November 2025.

sources.title: https://cylab.be/blog/463/use-thunderbird-to-fetch-your-outlook-365-emails
sources.claim: Owl for Exchange is a paid Thunderbird add-on at 10 EUR/year that syncs calendar and address books and supports MFA.

sources.title: https://www.betterbird.eu/
sources.claim: Betterbird's stable line in July 2026 is 140.13.0esr-bb25 (pre-EWS), while the newer 153.0esr-bb6 build carries a do-not-use-in-production warning.

sources.title: https://en.ittrip.xyz/microsoft-365/onenote-desktop-vs-web
sources.claim: Local (non-cloud) notebooks are a OneNote desktop-only feature; the web app is cloud-only.

sources.title: https://github.com/patrikx3/onenote
sources.claim: P3X OneNote is an actively released Electron wrapper of OneNote for Linux; 2026 releases added an 'Auto (system)' language option for locale detection.

sources.title: https://github.com/alxnbl/onenote-md-exporter
sources.claim: onenote-md-exporter is a Windows console app that exports OneNote notebooks to Markdown (via Word DOCX + Pandoc) with Joplin and Obsidian output targets.

sources.title: https://www.file2markdown.ai/blog/onenote-to-markdown
sources.claim: Known losses when exporting OneNote to Markdown in 2026: handwriting, text tags, password-protected sections and images nested in tables.

sources.title: https://rclone.org/commands/rclone_mount/
sources.claim: Without --vfs-cache-mode writes or full, an rclone mount cannot do random writes or seek-on-read, so many applications will not work with files on the mount.

sources.title: https://github.com/jstaf/onedriver
sources.claim: onedriver is a native FUSE filesystem for OneDrive giving on-demand file access; last pushed January 2026.

sources.title: https://www.insynchq.com/linux
sources.claim: Insync's own Linux page currently advertises OneDrive support including SharePoint, OneDrive for Business and Dropbox Team folders.

sources.title: https://github.com/abraunegg/onedrive/issues/2191
sources.claim: The abraunegg client's Entra app registration shows as unverified and requests broad delegated scopes, which is what tenant admins object to.

sources.title: https://github.com/abraunegg/onedrive/blob/master/docs/usage.md
sources.claim: Beyond interactive browser OAuth2, the client supports Intune SSO via the Microsoft Identity Device Broker D-Bus interface and the OAuth2 device authorisation flow for Entra ID.

sources.title: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/differences-between-using-a-workbook-in-the-browser-and-in-excel-f0dc28ed-b85d-4e1d-be6d-5878005db3b6
sources.claim: Excel for the web does not run macros, does not render ActiveX/form controls, and refuses to display workbooks with workbook-level IRM or digital signatures.

sources.title: https://www.onlyoffice.com/blog/2026/02/macros-or-ai-functions-understanding-onlyoffice-tools
sources.claim: ONLYOFFICE deliberately does not support VBA macros; its JavaScript macros are sandboxed with no system access.

sources.title: https://www.omgubuntu.co.uk/2026/02/libreoffice-26-2-new-features
sources.claim: LibreOffice 26.2 improves Excel interop: BIFF12 clipboard support removing paste size limits, Excel 2010-365 as the default XLSX export target, DOCX floating-table interop and partial OOXML chart-style round-tripping.

sources.title: https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/sbasic/shared/vbasupport.html
sources.claim: LibreOffice's own documentation states VBA support is incomplete and that users may need to rewrite macros in LibreOffice Basic; executable VBA requires enabling a Load/Save option.

sources.title: https://www.libreofficehelp.com/install-language-packs-libreoffice/
sources.claim: LibreOffice UI languages, spell checkers and help are installed as separate per-language packages on Linux and selected under Tools > Options > Language Settings > Languages.
